subtopic: Net Asset Value vs. Market Price
source_evidence: an ETF’s market price may reflect a premium or a discount to the ETF’s underlying value or NAV.
question: Misconception: An ETF’s market price is always the same as its net asset value (NAV).
answer: An ETF’s market price can differ from its NAV: it may be at a premium or a discount. As a result, you may pay more or less than NAV when buying shares, or receive more or less than NAV when selling them.
